summary: Rechecked 167 targets in 37 layers, all 223 citation occurrences, and 66 overlap claims. Three findings: two elliptic Picard targets confuse built divisor-class results with missing scheme line-bundle comparisons (high); the Habiro cohomology note overstates the canonical/all-degree exact-sequence scope (medium); the generic K₃ comparison is routed to the infinite-field indecomposable quotient instead of V.1 (medium).
checked: Independence and scope: the ledger attributes AUDIT-28 to claude4/2 and its accepted review REV-AUDIT-28 to claude2/1. Neither was this Codex session. Read the complete bot-confirmed issue, accepted result, accepted review and all five source roadmaps at explorer snapshot 36cd27dca40278121c895a72cd0bdc4ad42995b4. This attacks the accepted library audit, not every primary proof in the motivic area.

Rechecked all 37 assigned native layers and 167 targets: BorelRegulators 7/33; EllipticKTheory 8/34; EllipticRegulators 8/39; GeneralAlgebraicKTheory 10/42; HabiroNumberFields 4/19. The accepted classifications are 101 absent, 57 partial, 6 tauceti, 2 both and 1 mathlib. The newer KU readiness checkpoints are outside this audit batch and were not counted as omitted audit layers.

Read the actual statement and namespace/variable context of all 223 citation occurrences, including those attached to absent targets: 196 distinct library/file/name declarations in 136 files. All 136 cited files byte-match Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 or Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Also read the uncited comparison files needed by findings 1 and 2. No Lean compilation was run.

BorelRegulators: checked arithmetic-group/order/adelic ingredients, SL₂ reduction versus general reduction, continuous versus relative Lie cohomology and van Est, compact-dual/stability/Hurewicz/plus inputs, Borel ranks and regulator normalization, degree-one unit covolumes versus higher regulators, Dedekind zeta’s convergence/residue versus continuation and negative-integer leading terms, Tamagawa and Beilinson comparisons. Searched index names then both Lean trees under named and conceptual aliases; existing unit and Néron–Tate regulators do not provide higher K-regulators.

EllipticKTheory: checked projective-point quotients versus schemes, function-field isogenies and scheme comparison, categorical/ring K₀ versus scheme K₀, divisor classes versus line-bundle classes, localization/tame symbols/SK₁/coniveau, finite-field and projective-bundle computations, regular models versus minimal Weierstrass models, arithmetic integral parts and torsion-divisor principal functions. Searched alternate names in both libraries. Preserved the exact function-field torsion-divisor construction in E.7; finding 1 concerns its missing scheme/line-bundle bridge, not that theorem.

EllipticRegulators: checked lattice Weierstrass functions and their missing elliptic-manifold/uniformization comparison; abstract Hodge structures versus elliptic Betti/de Rham comparison; real Deligne complexes, differential forms, symbol pairings, elliptic dilogarithms and their logarithmic companions, Fourier/Gauss ingredients, CM/Hecke characters, integral-part and Beilinson conclusions, modular units/parametrizations and syntomic/Coleman inputs. Index-first and source searches found partial analytic/algebraic ingredients but no assembled regulator package; references to Coleman in documentation are not a Coleman integrator.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory: checked exact-structure axioms and small models, SpanBicat versus the Q-category, exact/split/abelian/triangulated K₀, finitely generated projective cofinality, scalar extension, higher K/plus/S constructions, projective-resolution versus general resolution, degree-zero versus all-degree additivity and invariance, nonconnective/relative/excision requirements, and product compatibility. Read the integrated partial decomposition’s summary, all 24 node statements/hypotheses/acceptance blocks and eight gaps. It is a plan, not implementation evidence. Source searches distinguish Quillen model categories and presheaf plus constructions from K-theory.

HabiroNumberFields: checked Bloch conventions, finite coefficients/Bockstein/Chern and norm-residue inputs; canonical versus explicit continuous-cohomology carriers; cyclotomic characters/units, Kummer injection versus isomorphism, S-unit/Selmer exact sequences, cyclic quantum dilogarithms, q-Pochhammer versus Euler products, completions and topologically nilpotent evaluation, local Frobenius gluing and K₃-indexed modules. Searched both pinned libraries under aliases. Existing function-field normResidue is not the norm-residue theorem; existing numerical Picard groups do not supply geometric Picard comparisons.

Read all 66 duplicate notes and full descriptions of their 54 distinct endpoints, plus V.1 as the corrected K₃ supplier. Checked relevant native stage edges, reserved-ID context and retirement resolution. All duplicate endpoints are current. Preserved genuine general-supplier/specialization relationships; finding 3 is a concrete carrier/domain mismatch. Known decomposition gaps were not promoted to new findings against this audit.

Programmatic consistency checks: assigned native stage sets equal the 37 audited layers; every audited target, note, status and duplicate list agrees with the reviewed library-coverage projection, including its evidence cap. Rechecked the citation counts and pinned file hashes. Searches covered missing components as well as wholly absent targets; none of the three findings rests only on a failed name search.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-28.result.json: EllipticKTheory:E.2, targets 3 and 4 (degree splitting and Pic⁰(E)); associated summary and upstream-overlap note
findings.claim: The two targets are marked tauceti, with more-general/exact evidence, although the cited declarations concern abstract or function-field divisor classes. E.2 needs Picard classes of line bundles on the projective scheme over the base field. The missing comparison is not supplied by either cited theorem, so these are partial inputs to the roadmap targets, not completed targets.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/CBirkbeck/tauceti-explorer/blob/36cd27dca40278121c895a72cd0bdc4ad42995b4/content/campaign/EllipticKTheory/README.md#L26-L41 places the Picard statements between the scheme rank–determinant computation and its tensor-product multiplication. The explicit contract in data/atlas.json, stage KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.5, is on line-bundle classes over the base field. At the pinned Tau Ceti commit, https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilDivisor/Degree/Splitting.lean#L227 has codomain picZero w h × ℤ for an OrderSystem and a weight-one point. https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/FunctionField/DivisorClass.lean#L79 has type W.Point ≃+ (Divisor.degreeClass W.isFunctionField).ker, assuming a Dedekind coordinate ring; it does not mention a scheme or LineBundleClass. The relevant scheme comparison https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilDivisor/Scheme/LineBundle.lean#L108 is a map from scheme divisor classes to LineBundleClass, proved injective at line 140. Its opening documentation explicitly leaves surjectivity open. https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/WeilDivisor/Scheme/TensorProduct.lean#L405-L429 proves addition/tensor compatibility and bundles an additive homomorphism, not an equivalence. The audit itself acknowledges in E.1 that the Weierstrass projective scheme and function-field comparison are missing, and in E.2 target 2 that line-bundle degree is missing. These missing bridges prevent substituting the cited divisor-class equivalences into E.2.
findings.fix: Change both E.2 targets to partial and describe the existing abstract splitting and elliptic function-field dictionary precisely. Retain those declarations as reusable components, with related evidence relative to the full line-bundle targets; add the existing injective divisor-to-line-bundle comparison and tensor compatibility as further partial evidence. Leave the projective scheme/function-field/divisor dictionary, surjectivity onto line-bundle classes, degree compatibility and elliptic specialization explicitly outstanding. Reuse the existing ModularCurves/JacobianChallenge direction for the general bridges and E.2 for its specialization; do not rebuild the proved function-field result. Recompute the E.2 layer verdict under the audit convention (its two fully built targets have become partial), and qualify the summary and upstream EllipticCurves Layer 0 overlap note. Keep the already-correct absent K₀ conclusions unchanged.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-28.result.json: HabiroNumberFields:HB.1, target 2, note on continuous Galois cohomology and its long exact sequence
findings.claim: The note presents the long exact sequence as built on Mathlib’s canonical ContinuousCohomology. The pinned sequence is instead in TauCeti.ContCohomology’s explicit discrete-coefficient model in degrees zero through two. The canonical comparison is proved only in degree zero; the cited all-degree restriction map does not supply this comparison or an all-degree exact sequence.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Coefficients.lean#L195 defines kummerShortExact as a DiscreteShortExact in the explicit coefficient framework. https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LongExact.lean#L13-L31 displays 0 → H⁰(A) → H⁰(B) → H⁰(C) → H¹(A) → H¹(B) → H¹(C) → H²(A) → H²(B); its final theorem explicitLongExact_H2B at line 546 is an equality of range and kernel for explicitCoeff2. https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/ContinuousCohomologyIso.lean#L141 constructs explicitH0IsoContinuousCohomology only, into continuousCohomology 0 (ofDiscreteModule ℤ G M). Lines 55–68 explain the missing positive-degree passage between iterated continuous-map cochains and functions on powers of G. The audit’s other citation, https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Functoriality.lean#L127, is res for canonical cohomology, not an exactness theorem. Whole-index and whole-source searches found only the degree-zero canonical bridge. GroupCohomologyIso.lean does prove H¹/H² comparisons, but to abstract groupCohomology under a discrete-group hypothesis, not the canonical continuous carrier for general profinite G.
findings.fix: Keep target 2 partial. Replace the note with separate statements: canonical continuous cohomology and restriction exist; the explicit discrete-module H⁰/H¹/H² model has the displayed low-degree exact sequence and the Kummer short exact sequence; the canonical comparison is currently degree zero only. Cite LongExact.lean and explicitH0IsoContinuousCohomology for those limits. Record higher-degree exactness and the positive-degree canonical comparison as remaining work when the consumer requires them, using the existing ProfiniteCohomology owner. Preserve the already-built explicit Kummer map/injectivity in HB.2; do not replan it.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-28.result.json: GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2 and GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2:low-degree-comparisons, duplicate entries pointing to K3BlochGroups:V.4
findings.claim: Both overlap notes identify Suslin’s V.4 exact sequence with the explicit K₃ comparison requested for rings. V.4 treats the indecomposable quotient for infinite fields. The actual general-ring comparison K₃(A) ≅ H₃(St(A),ℤ) is owned by V.1, which is missing from these duplicate lists. Thus following the audit sends the general target to the wrong supplier.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/CBirkbeck/tauceti-explorer/blob/36cd27dca40278121c895a72cd0bdc4ad42995b4/content/campaign/GeneralAlgebraicKTheory/README.md, K.2 and K.2:low-degree-comparisons, requests the explicit K₁, K₂ and K₃ comparisons and separately identifies Matsumoto as field-specific. In the same snapshot, data/atlas.json stage K3BlochGroups:V.1 (source content/campaign/K3BlochGroups/README.md lines 16–25) explicitly constructs K₃(A) ≅ H₃(St(A),ℤ), bar cycles and naturality for ring maps. V.4 (lines 49–61) instead has 0 → enhanced Tor(μ(F),μ(F)) → K₃^ind(F) → B_Sus(F) → 0 for infinite fields, with a comparison back to V.1. This is a quotient comparison, not a presentation of full K₃ for general rings. Weibel, K-book IV §1 after Corollary 1.7.1 and Exercise 1.9, https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.IV.pdf#page=6 and #page=15, supplies the general-ring homological comparison. The integrated GeneralAlgebraicKTheory decomposition also leaves the explicit low-degree comparisons as an import gap; it does not turn V.4 into the generic supplier.
findings.fix: Replace the V.4 duplicate entry in both stages with K3BlochGroups:V.1 and describe its homological K₃ comparison. V.4 may remain a separately qualified downstream reference for the infinite-field indecomposable quotient, but not as the supplier of the generic target. Correct the inherited atlas prerequisite V.4 → K.2:low-degree-comparisons to V.1 for that generic comparison through the maintainer/integration route. Retain the absent library statuses and the existing K₁/K₂ suppliers; no new K₃ roadmap or duplicate construction is needed.
